# The model: structure

Trained on 506 matches. Every fitted model answers one question and appears once. Each input has a kind: **context** (fixed for the match) and **state** (the situation now) are adjustment and never a fix; **decision** (a choice the team made) and **execution** (how well it was carried out) are the only candidates for "what should have been done" and "what went wrong". What the other team did during the same window is measured beside a node, never fitted. An input that predicts the previous result as well as the next **marks the situation** and is never a fix. Every link's status comes from refitting without it on matches the model never saw.

## How to read the tables

- **Gain**: how much worse the node predicts matches it never saw when that cause group's inputs are left out (log loss for yes/no nodes, seconds of typical error for number nodes); ± is the spread across the six held-out groups of matches. **Status**: *supported* = the gain is more than twice its spread; *rejected* = leaving the group out predicts better by that much; *not clear yet* = anything between, so read it as a lead. A supported group with a small gain is real but small.

- **Reading**: the node's curve for that input, in points of result chance for an otherwise even case (yes/no nodes) or in seconds (number nodes), at the input's low end and at its high end. Example: *damage against the usual, own minus enemy (-28.8 points at -15.4..-2.0; +27.9 at 1.9..13.2)* means a team out-damaging the usual by 2 to 13 per second had about 28 points more chance of winning the fight than an even case, and a team under it by that much about 29 points less.

- **Kind**: context (fixed for the match), state (the situation now), decision (a choice the team made), execution (how the play was carried out). Only decision and execution inputs can be a fix; **[marks the situation]** flags an input that predicts the previous result as well as the next, so it describes the spot rather than causing the result; an **allocation** decision (how many to send, escort, defend with) carries the flag but may still be a fix (R-282); **[reads backwards]** flags an execution input whose curve runs against its expected direction, read as a reaction to the result coming (disabling more because the kill is not coming), never a fault or a fix (R-285). **Cap**: the number of inputs the node's data can carry (one per 20 of the rarer outcome); over the cap, inputs are pruned in order (Claude's unclear, Claude's rejected, approved discoveries unclear, Denning's unclear; R-278); supported inputs and those Denning ruled to keep are never pruned.

- Every node says whose side its rows are read from ("Read from ..."): "own" and "enemy" in its inputs follow that side, and so does what a high result means.

- Nodes that look alike are the same event read from a different side or at a different moment, by design: *run outcome* (the running team), *run defence* (the defending team, every run) and *capture speed* (captures only, how long); *flag answer* (how well one answering run was executed) and *flag swing* (how the lead moves over a minute). A node's result can be another node's input (split answer feeds split effect and collapse): that is how chains are followed back.

- **Denning** in a definition column is the player whose rulings define the engine's terms (docs/RULINGS.md); "Claude's, to confirm" marks a detection rule Claude wrote that he has not yet ruled on.

## Glossary (the measured terms in game language)

- **morale**: death penalty and boosts, in percent of maximum health, summed over a team's eight players (-60 to +10 each); "own minus enemy" is the gap
- **stand**: who holds the flag stand: 1 own team, 0 nobody, -1 the enemy
- **flag lead**: seconds the team is ahead (+) or behind (-) in the flag exchange: how much sooner than the enemy it could capture next
- **boost clock**: seconds until the stand holder's next morale boost (every 2 minutes held): + when own boost is coming, - when the enemy's is, 0 when nobody holds
- **time down**: enemy minus own seconds until all dead players are back: positive means the enemy has more time down than own team, so more is good for own team
- **seconds until the first defender arrived**: counted from the split entering the base; negative means a defender was already there or arrived before the split entered; 60 means nobody came within a minute
- **who carries (runner class)**: a label, not a scale: 0 warrior, 1 dervish, 2 assassin, 3 paragon, 4 ranger, 5 elementalist, 6 mesmer, 7 necromancer, 8 ritualist, 9 monk; read the curve as one reading per class
- **escorts**: players travelling with the carrier; a run with many escorts is usually a contested run, so more escorts can read as a slower capture
- **main**: the team's main group (players within 2,500 units of each other, not splitting or running)
- **players within one spike**: players whose health, after death penalty, an enemy spike build could take in one spike (DP stacking)
- **turtling**: the team holding inside its own base or pit (share of live players at home)
- **pit pressure**: players of each side within 500 units of a pit, own minus enemy
- **team strength gap**: the measured rating gap between the two guilds (fitted rating blended with the lineup who played); 400 points is about 10 to 1 odds
- **the usual**: the median for that role across every stored fight (damage per second on players), so output is judged against what that role normally does
- **value (of an enchantment or hex)**: its measured output: recorded damage, healing and prevented damage per second while up, plus the drop in the bearer's output after a strip
- **pit NPC value**: the pit NPCs alive priced in win points (knights, archers, Bodyguard) from the win model
- **snare, speed and escape power**: from the bar's skills at the player's attribute rank: slow fraction x seconds x uses per minute (snares), speed bonus x seconds x uses per minute (speed), Shadow Steps (escapes); measured seconds replace the formula once a skill has 15+ uses
- **skill-seconds disabled**: for each enemy skill disabled by Complicate, Power Lock, Power Block or Blackout, the seconds it stayed disabled, added up
- **pip-seconds**: health degeneration put on the enemy: pips (2 health per second each) x seconds, added up
- **health ceiling**: maximum health after death penalty (what a spike has to get through)
- **backup flag, waiting runner**: a second flag held near the stand while your team holds it; a runner standing at the spawn ready for the next flag
- **flag model**: the engine's estimate of how many seconds each team needs to capture next, from carrier positions, speeds and spawns
- **distance**: game units: 1,000 is about the aggro bubble's radius; a spell's cast range is about 1,250; a flag run is 4,000 to 9,000
- **the 28:00 tiebreak**: a match that reaches 28:00 goes to the team that dealt more Lord damage
- **split depth**: the nearest split member's distance to the defending pit: smaller is deeper into the base

## Tier 2: decision nodes (the macro answer)

| Kind | Moment | Choices | Definition |
|---|---|---|---|
| enemy_pickup | the enemy picks up a new flag | already running; ran (within 25 s); held | Denning |
| split_in_base | an enemy split enters the base | collapsed; defended without a collapse; missed (speed: on time 15 s, late, missed 60 s) | Denning |
| power_play | a numbers advantage at main, away from home, damage traded (any size) | pushed; held | Denning |
| boost_clock | the enemy's boost is 30 s away | running; not running (with the players' first action) | Denning |
| after_wipe | the team just won a wipe | pushed the pit; took the flag; reset | Denning |
| late_game | 24:00 | players at the enemy Lord, in levels | Denning |
| split_or_stay | every 30 s from 1:00, 6+ alive, not splitting | split within 30 s; stayed | Denning |
| runner_choice | a fresh run from the spawn (holds left out) | who carries (class) | Denning |
| offence_or_defence | a fight starts (first 15 s) | offensive (disruption on enemy healers); defensive (on midline and frontline); mixed | Denning (R-279) |
| eight_v_eight_or_flag | the enemy picks up, own team 7+ alive (a power play when not up on flags) | commit all 8; flag game | Denning (R-279) |
| who_defends | a split enters the base | first defender's class (Mes/A, frontline, 8 Monk or healer, midline), alone or with a collapse | Denning (R-279) |
| npcs_or_dp | 3+ kills at or past the enemy footmen | NPCs; DP (players); both | Denning (R-280) |
| play_for_28_or_lord | from 10:00 every 60 s, a team that has taken enemy NPCs | push for the kill; play for 28 | Denning (R-281) |

Cases per kind in the usual play (last report): after_wipe 1183, boost_clock 1841, eight_v_eight_or_flag 4374, enemy_pickup 6098, late_game 164, npcs_or_dp 296, offence_or_defence 1274, play_for_28_or_lord 4046, power_play 4646, runner_choice 4218, split_in_base 999, split_or_stay 17779, who_defends 899.

## Tier 4: the win model

55,154 rows (one per team per 15 s), 506 matches, 33 variables in use. Held out by whole match: log loss 0.382 against 0.475 for strength alone; accuracy 84% against 78%.

Importance = the variable's average absolute contribution to the win chance across every row, in log-odds (0.8 is large, 0.1 small); it says how much the variable moves the reading, not which way. Direction = the sign of its curve from low to high value, read on "Win-probability model" (+ means more of it raises own win chance).

## Waiting list (not in any model)

proposal: 4

- proposal: run_outcome, capture_speed control on the runner by distance to the stand: R-288: control, damage and pushes received read as a reaction because runs that get far get hit; measure them by distance band (far from the stand v near) or before the halfway point, so both run nodes and capture speed read the control where it mattered
- proposal: flag_answer, run_outcome flag dropped by a Shadow Step: R-289: a Shadow Step drops the flag now; a runner who uses one is an execution fault, not a speed asset (replacement for the retired runner_escapes)
- proposal: fight_outcome (values.py) hex value incl. trigger damage: R-290: trigger hexes (Mind Wrack) leave the target when they fire, so time-on-player undervalues them; value a hex by its recorded output incl. the damage on trigger or removal and the energy pressure it stands for; and a harmless hex left on is not a fault
- proposal: pit_npc_loss, lord_damage NPC healing by target and kind: R-291: split npc_healing_10s by which NPC was healed (archer, knight, Bodyguard, Lord; under AoE or not) and by heal kind (direct v enchantment), so the data can test the common wisdom (archer over knight under AoE, Bodyguard over Lord) and whether enchantment heals on the Lord cost Lord damage
